confirmed.title: A dataset squeezed down to 0-d loses its dtype on read (byte order, fixed-length string width); /array/block and zarr chunk endpoints then serve wrong bytes
confirmed.file: tiled/ndslice.py:579-595 (expand_for_shape squeeze= turns each length-1 slice into an integer) + tiled/adapters/hdf5.py:262-264 (_read returns the h5py read as is)
confirmed.failing_input: HDF5 dataset be = numpy.array([256,258,260], dtype='>i2') or s5 = numpy.array([b'hello',b'ab',b'xyz'], dtype='S5'); registered with parameters {'dataset': name, 'slice': '1:2', 'squeeze': True} (structure shape (), dtype >i2 / S5)
confirmed.expected: adapter.read() returns a 0-d array with the structure dtype (>i2 / S5), as PR #2 did; client.read_block(()) -> 258 / b'ab'; GET /zarr/v2/<key>/0 chunk payload 0102 / 6162000000
confirmed.actual: adapter.read() returns dtype <i2 / S2 (h5py integer-index read returns a native-endian, null-stripped numpy scalar). /api/v1/array/block/<key>?block= (octet-stream) and /zarr/v2|v3 chunks serialize it as is: client.read_block(()) -> array(513, dtype='>i2') (big-endian 258 decoded as 513; >f8 262.0 decoded as 3.12e-317); for S5 -> ValueError: buffer size must be a multiple of element size; zarr chunk payload 0201 / 6162 under a .zarray that declares >i2 / S5. /array/full is correct (router applies numpy.asarray(..., dtype=structure dtype)). Same for vlen strings (served as S5).

confirmed.severity: medium (silent wrong values over HTTP; narrow: squeeze/registration to a 0-d structure AND non-native byte order or string dtype, AND read via /array/block, client.read_block or zarr; the integer-slice registration path, e.g. slice='1', already had this defect in PR #2 and still has it)
confirmed.suggested_fix: in HDF5ArrayAdapter._read cast the result to the dataset dtype (numpy.asarray(array, dtype=self._array.dtype)), which also fixes the pre-existing slice='<int>' case

confirmed.title: NDSlice.is_expanded now accepts an UNexpanded reversed slice with a negative stop, so compose_slices silently returns a wrong composition (PR #2 raised ValueError)
confirmed.file: tiled/ndslice.py:491-497 (_is_absolute) with _slice_range:107-119 treating any negative stop as 'to the start'
confirmed.failing_input: NDSlice(slice(5, -3, -1))[NDSlice(slice(0, 3))] for an axis of length 10 (numpy: arange(10)[5:-3:-1] is empty)
confirmed.expected: ValueError('Composition of slices with undetermined shape is not supported.') as in PR #2, or a composition equivalent to arr[5:-3:-1][0:3] == []
confirmed.actual: (slice(5, 2, -1),) selecting [5, 4, 3]; NDSlice(slice(5,-3,-1))[NDSlice(0)] -> (5,) instead of an error
confirmed.severity: low / latent: no in-tree caller passes such a left operand (HDF5 expands its stencil; brute force over 119,808 ndindex-expanded slices shows _slice_range matches Python semantics for every expanded slice; Zarr stencil and read_block block slices are forward)

behaviour_differences_vs_pr2.what: Negative-step requests/registrations whose start is below -n (e.g. ?slice=-11:2:-1 on 10 rows, -9::-1, ::-1,-3::-1): PR #2 returned wrong data (dask 2026.8.0 mis-normalizes raw reversed slices: 2664 of 14400 raw reversed slices wrong vs numpy; 0 of 60000 ndindex-expanded ones), head returns the numpy result (empty).
behaviour_differences_vs_pr2.http_visible: yes on raw HTTP /array/full (PR #2: 200 with 7 wrong elements; head: 200 empty or, for >=2-D empties with octet-stream, 500 from a PRE-EXISTING serializer bug: memoryview(...).cast('B') raises TypeError for any >=2-D empty array, also at PR #2 for ?slice=2:2). The Python client short-circuits empty expected shapes, so it never sees the difference.

behaviour_differences_vs_pr2.what: Registered structure itself for such slices: from_uris with e.g. slice='-3::-1' on a length-1 axis gives shape (0,...) at head vs (1,...) at PR #2.

Error precedence: an invalid request on a node whose structure no longer matches the data raises IndexError at head (request validated against the structure first) where PR #2 raised DataNotReadyError / IncompatibleShapeError / NotImplementedError / TypeError from force_reshape or dask.
behaviour_differences_vs_pr2.http_visible: yes, status code on /array/full: head 400 vs PR #2 503/422/500

behaviour_differences_vs_pr2.what: Zero-size registered arrays with a mismatched catalog structure (notready/incompatible): head computes the correct empty registered array and force_reshape's size-equality rule reshapes it (200 empty), PR #2 computed a wrong non-empty array (dask bug) and raised IncompatibleShapeError; occasionally the reverse (dask reshape NotImplementedError on empty arrays at head where PR #2's wrong shape happened to fit).
behaviour_differences_vs_pr2.http_visible: yes but only for zero-size structures
behaviour_differences_vs_pr2.verdict: edge, follows from the dask fix

behaviour_differences_vs_pr2.what: Return type of 0-d results: head returns a numpy scalar for a squeezed scalar dataset and 0-d ndarrays for all-integer requests where PR #2 returned numpy scalars (and vice versa).
behaviour_differences_vs_pr2.http_visible: no for numeric native dtypes (216 HTTP responses compared byte for byte; scalar /array/full, /array/block, zarr v2/v3 identical). The dtype part is confirmed bug 1.

behaviour_differences_vs_pr2.what: Non-string slice parameter: slice=0 (int) was ignored by PR #2 (falsy) and is applied by head; a node registered under PR #2 with slice=0 (structure (4,3)) now raises IncompatibleShapeError on read. slice=[1,2] (list) was a fancy row index in PR #2 and is a tuple index (1,2) at head.
behaviour_differences_vs_pr2.http_visible: yes (422) if a catalog stores slice as a JSON int/list; tilewright stores str(int); the annotated type is str | NDSlice | None

behaviour_differences_vs_pr2.what: ZarrArrayAdapter (writable arrays) via the rewritten compose_slices: an empty reversed request such as slice(-11, 2, -1) now composes to slice(0,0) and returns [] instead of zarr's NegativeStepError; other negative steps still raise NegativeStepError in both.
behaviour_differences_vs_pr2.http_visible: yes, only for empty reversed requests on writable (zarr) arrays
